html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. MCP: Model Context Protocol; NDA: non-disclosure agreement

  • A time plan for 53 items in 120 minutes
  • How to read an item, find the binding constraint and eliminate distractors
  • Multiple-response tactics
  • Policies and logistics, and what happens after the exam

2Time Plan

Phase Time What to do
First pass about 80 min Answer what you know in about 90 seconds per item; mark doubtful items
Second pass about 30 min Return to marked items; use elimination
Final check about 10 min Every item answered; every multiple-response item has the required number of selections
  • With 53 items in 120 minutes you have about 2 minutes 15 seconds per item: do not spend more than two minutes on one before marking it.
  • The guide describes no deduction for wrong answers: answer every item.
Exam tip

Mark a hard item and move on: it costs the time of two easy ones.

3Reading an Item

  1. Read the last sentence first ("Which approach best...?") and note the number of answers to select.
  2. Find the binding constraint in the stem: latency, cost, security, reliability, compliance, maintainability.
  3. Predict the answer before you read the options.
Word in the stem Points to...
"overnight", "non-urgent", "cost is the primary concern" Batch
"users wait", "interactive" Realtime (and streaming)
"same prefix every request" Caching
"shared across several applications", "maintained independently" MCP server
"procedure", "checklist", "expertise" Skill
"must never", "destructive" Hook or deny rule
"untrusted", "hidden instructions", "third-party content" Data separation, least privilege, screening
"keys", "credentials" Secrets manager, rotation, server-side use
"unexpected wrong answers" Check what the model received; traces; evals
Exam tip

The cause is usually stated in the stem (a log line, a number, what the application sends): use it before choosing a fix.

4Eliminating Distractors

  • Cross out answers that do not address the stated constraint (a bigger model for a security problem).
  • Cross out over-engineering when a simple fix has not been tried (a classifier before better descriptions).
  • Cross out absolute claims that ignore evals ("always the largest model").
  • Cross out answers that leave secrets in code, prompts or browsers.
  • Between two valid answers, choose the enforced, measured, least-privileged, cost-aware one.

Multiple-response items

  • Choose exactly the number the stem asks for; judge each option on its own against the requirement.
  • If you find one clear answer, the second is often the companion safeguard rather than a repeat of the first.
Exam tip

When two answers both work, prefer the one that is enforced in code, measured by evals and least privileged.

5Policies and Logistics

Topic What to know
Registration Through the Anthropic Partner Academy and Pearson VUE; online proctored or test center
Reschedule or cancel Up to 24 hours before; later changes forfeit the fee
ID Valid government photo ID; the name must match the registration exactly
Accommodations Request and get approval from Pearson VUE before scheduling
Agreements You accept a confidentiality and non-disclosure agreement; never share exam content
Retakes 14 / 30 / 90 days; max 4 attempts per rolling 12 months
Result Pass or fail and scaled score, plus percent correct per domain
Validity 12 months from the award date

[Verify live] The guide is version 1.0 (July 2026); updated guides and exam content are announced for November and December 2026. Check the Partner Academy for the current guide, fee and eligibility before you book. As of 8 November 2026.

6Final Review Checklist

  • I can state the ten decision rules without looking.
  • I know realtime versus batch, caching rules, effort and thinking, and the error codes.
  • I can choose between workflow and agent, and between built-in tool, custom tool, Skill and MCP.
  • I know the model tiers and how to select and pin a model.
  • I can explain prompt injection defenses, least privilege, hooks and key management.
  • I know context engineering techniques and output validation.
  • I can debug by classifying the failure and isolating the layer.
  • I have built a small Claude application with a tool, a prompt, validation and an eval.

The last week

  • Seven to four days before: reread the notes of the heaviest domains (Applications and Integration, then Model Selection, then Agents) and redo their scenario questions; write down every item you got wrong and why.
  • Three days before: work through the Decision Chooser in Module 17 aloud, naming the deciding question for each row; reread the Names and Values table.
  • The day before: light review only: the ten decision rules, the error codes and the time plan. Check your ID, registration name and test setup, and sleep.
  • On the day: arrive or log in early, read each item's last sentence first, and keep to the time plan.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Time ~90 s per item first pass; mark and return; check multiple-response counts
Method Last sentence first · binding constraint · predict · eliminate
Pick Enforced · measured · least-privileged · cost-aware
Logistics Photo ID with exact name · 24-hour change rule · NDA · retakes 14/30/90 days · valid 12 months
